findings.quote: for 45 s or until a front door is opened
findings.explanation: WLC-023 allows window movement after ignition off for 60 s, while this requirement allows 45 s. Both cannot be true. WLC-023 also lacks the door-open condition.
findings.rewrite: After ignition off, the controller shall allow window movement for [TBD: confirm 45 s or 60 s] or until a front door is opened, whichever comes first.

findings.explanation: "Quickly" is not measurable. The requirement also does not say whether the window closes fully or how soon after the rain report it starts.
findings.rewrite: When the rain sensor reports rain, the window shall close fully within [TBD: maximum close time] of the report.

findings.quote: shall be disabled when the controller is not normalized
findings.explanation: WLC-016 requires anti-pinch protection in manual mode, but manual mode can run while not normalized, where this requirement disables it. Disabling a safety function also needs a clear reason.
findings.rewrite: [TBD: decide whether anti-pinch is active in manual mode when not normalized, and align WLC-016 and WLC-017 with that decision.]

findings.explanation: "Robust" and "all disturbances" cannot be verified, since no test can cover every disturbance.
findings.rewrite: The anti-pinch function shall not trigger a false pinch detection under [TBD: list of defined disturbances, e.g. road vibration profile] and shall still detect a pinch above 100 N under the same conditions.

findings.explanation: WLC-007 gives 45 s (and ends on front door open) for the same condition, so the two disagree. The requirement is also partly a duplicate of WLC-007.
findings.rewrite: Delete WLC-023 and keep WLC-007 with the agreed time of [TBD: 45 s or 60 s].

findings.quote: exceeds the limit, the controller shall reduce motor current to a safe value
findings.explanation: Neither the temperature limit nor the reduced current value is given, so the behavior cannot be tested. The limit's relation to the 140 °C in WLC-026 is also unclear.
findings.rewrite: When the estimated motor temperature exceeds [TBD: current-reduction temperature], the controller shall reduce motor current to no more than [TBD: reduced current in A].

findings.quote: shall store diagnostic trouble code B1A01 when the Hall sensor signal is missing for more than 200 ms while the motor is driven, and shall stop the motor
findings.explanation: Storing the DTC and stopping the motor are two separate behaviors. The stop has no time limit.
findings.rewrite: WLC-029a: The controller shall store DTC B1A01 when the Hall sensor signal is missing for more than 200 ms while the motor is driven. WLC-029b: In that case the controller shall stop the motor within [TBD: stop time].

findings.quote: shall store diagnostic trouble code B1A02 when motor current exceeds 25 A for more than 50 ms and shall stop the motor and shall set the fault state in WLC_Status
findings.explanation: It combines three behaviors (store DTC, stop motor, set CAN fault state) that should be tested separately. The stop has no time limit.
findings.rewrite: WLC-030a: The controller shall store DTC B1A02 when motor current exceeds 25 A for more than 50 ms. WLC-030b: In that case the controller shall stop the motor within [TBD: stop time]. WLC-030c: In that case the controller shall set the fault state in WLC_Status.

findings.quote: In sleep mode, the controller shall draw less than 100 µA from the 12 V supply.
findings.explanation: It repeats WLC-004 word for word.
"User friendly" has no measurable meaning and no test could show it is met.
findings.rewrite: [TBD: replace with measurable usability requirements, e.g. a defined switch feedback or a task success rate in a user test.]

findings.quote: The software shall be developed according to the company software process.
findings.explanation: It is about how the software is developed, not about product behavior. It also does not name the process.
findings.rewrite: Move to the project plan or quality plan, citing [TBD: process document and version].
